children: Brokerage and wealth-management group Charles Schwab

fell to $93.17, down approximately 3.8%, as of 11:17 a.m. ET on October 15, as investors weighed its quarterly earnings. Investor's Business Daily reported the post-earnings decline. Record client inflows gave Schwab plenty to celebrate. The tougher question: how much of that new money will turn into recurring revenue?

Schwab reported quarterly revenue of $7.171 billion, up 16.9% from a year earlier, alongside $190.4 billion in core net new assets. Net interest revenue climbed to $3.476 billion from $3.050 billion, supplying roughly 41% of the total revenue increase. Asset-management and administration fees rose 14.3% to $1.913 billion. Interest income carried substantial weight, but fee growth pulled its share.

The valuation chart puts the shares just 1.23% above the $92.03 GF Value estimate, suggesting little gap against that benchmark after the selloff. That leaves execution in focus. Schwab needs to turn incoming assets into durable fees while protecting interest income as funding costs and asset yields shift. Record inflows open the door. The revenue those assets generate will determine how much the business benefits.

title: Schwab Stocks Fall 3.8% Although Record Inflows Leave an Interest-Income Test
